name: Vehicle Re-Identification in Context
description: Existing vehicle re-identification (re-id) evaluation benchmarks consider strongly artificial test scenarios by assuming the availability of high quality images and fine-grained appearance at an almost constant image scale, reminiscent to images required for Automatic Number Plate Recognition, e.g. VeRi-776. Such assumptions are often invalid in realistic vehicle re-id scenarios where arbitrarily changing image resolutions (scales) are the norm. This makes the existing vehicle re-id benchmarks limited for testing the true performance of a re-id method. In this work, we introduce a more realistic and challenging vehicle re-id benchmark, called Vehicle Re-Identification in Context (VRIC). In contrast to existing datasets, VRIC is uniquely characterised by vehicle images subject to more realistic and unconstrained variations in resolution (scale), motion blur, illumination, occlusion, and viewpoint. evaluation_method: rank-based retrieval metrics (e.g., CMC / Rank-1, mAP)
reputation: A well-known vehicle re-identification benchmark used to test robustness under realistic scale, blur, occlusion, and viewpoint variation.
notes: Non-LLM vision benchmark; challenging due to unconstrained resolution/scale changes and other real-world degradations.
